headline: Acquisitions drive strong growth, profit and margins
summary_short: Crane's Q2 2026 sales rose 25.6% y/y to $724.7M as acquisitions added $114.5M and core sales grew 5.2% on pricing; operating profit jumped 40.2% to $144.3M on tariff refunds and productivity, lifting diluted EPS 10.9% to $1.63.
summary_long: Q2 2026 net sales grew 25.6% y/y to $724.7M: acquisitions (Druck, Panametrics, Reuter-Stokes, Optek) added $114.5M, core sales rose 5.2% on pricing, and FX added 0.6%. Operating profit rose 40.2% to $144.3M as productivity/cost savings, net price, and an $18.7M tariff refund outweighed unfavorable mix; operating margin expanded to 19.9% from 17.8%. Net income rose 11.0% to $95.9M — PY's $86.4M included $6.1M of now-divested discontinued-operations income, so underlying growth stronger. Long-term debt fell to $1,087.1M from $1,192.6M q/q as Crane repaid $100M on its revolver after drawing $50M to help fund $1,355.4M of H1 acquisitions. FY2026: total sales guided to mid-20%s growth, core sales at the higher end of 5-6%.

drivers.explanation: Sales grew on acquisitions (Druck, Panametrics, Reuter-Stokes, Optek) adding $114.5M (19.8%), core sales up $30.0M (5.2%) driven by higher pricing, and $3.0M of favorable FX translation.
Gross margin ticked up as cost of sales grew slower (+24.6%) than revenue (+25.6%), helped by $18.7M of tariff refunds and $13.6M of productivity gains offsetting acquisition and mix cost increases.

Operating profit rose on productivity/cost savings ($21.4M), strong net price ($16.4M), and an $18.7M tariff refund tied to a 2026 Supreme Court IEEPA ruling, partly offset by unfavorable mix (-$15.5M).
Operating margin expanded because operating profit grew faster (+40.2%) than revenue (+25.6%) — the tariff refund and cost discipline outpaced acquisition dilution and mix headwinds.

The filing's own comparison shows continuing-operations net income up 19.4% ($95.9M vs $80.3M); the smaller 11.0% total-basis growth reflects the prior year's $6.1M of discontinued-operations income that no longer recurs.
Net margin fell because revenue grew faster (+25.6%) than total net income (+11.0%) — the gap traces to the prior-year discontinued-operations income drop-off, not weaker operating performance.
Basic EPS grew as diluted-basic share count was nearly flat y/y (57.7M vs 57.5M) and no shares were repurchased this quarter, so earnings growth flowed straight through to EPS.
Diluted EPS growth mirrors basic EPS: diluted share count was nearly flat y/y (58.7M vs 58.5M) and Crane made no open-market repurchases this quarter.

Long-term debt fell q/q after Crane repaid $100 million under its Revolving Facility in Q2, having drawn $50 million in Q1 for working capital; H1 acquisitions of $1,355.4M were funded largely by debt raised earlier in the year.

Sales and profit surged on four 2026 acquisitions (Druck, Panametrics, Reuter-Stokes, Optek) plus a one-time $18.7M tariff refund; FY2026 guidance points to mid-20%s total sales growth with core sales at the higher end of its 5-6% long-term target.
